title: Caring for porcelain stoneware: simple rules
excerpt: Porcelain stoneware is one of the most durable finishes, yet proper care keeps its look for years. A short guide to daily cleaning and joints.
body:
Porcelain stoneware absorbs almost no water and resists stains and scratches. That makes it one of the most practical finishes for homes, offices and public spaces. Yet, like any material, it needs a little attention.

For daily cleaning, warm water and a neutral detergent are enough. Avoid acidic or harsh abrasive products; they harm the joints more than the surface. Use a soft cloth or microfibre on polished finishes.

The first clean after installation is especially important. Grout residue must be removed before it dries. Otherwise a dull film remains on the surface and is harder to remove later.

Joints are the most vulnerable part of the finish. Inspect them from time to time and renew them when needed. In wet rooms, a moisture-resistant grout is recommended.

On relief and textured tiles (for example, in TORRA collections) dust can gather in the recesses. A soft brush gives good results here.

A mat in the entrance area holds back sand and small stones, the simplest way to protect the surface from scratches.
